sub_senses.label: (l)
sub_senses.heading: where knowledge of a person's greatness is widespread

quotations.old_english: His hlīsa āsprang tō Syrian lande
Āsprang his hlīsa geond þā land wīde
Gif hæleða hwone hlīsan lyste
Sē þe wile wīslīce æfter þām hlīsan spyrian, þonne ongit he swīþe hraþe hū lytel hē bið
Heora gemynd onweg gewāt mid þām myclan hlīsan
quotations.english: the memory of them passed away along with the great fame (? the Latin is: Periit memoria eorum cum sonitu)

quotations.old_english: Gē þone hlīsan habban tiliaþ ofer þióda mā þonne eów þearf sié

sub_senses.heading: where a certain character is attributed to a person

quotations.old_english: Sint tō manienne þā þe yfel dēgellīce dōð and gōd openlīce, þæt hī geþencen hū hrædlīce se eorþlica hlīsa ofergæð (humana judicia quanta velocitate evolant)
Gōd word and gōd hlīsa ælces monnes biþ betera þonne ænig wēla
Iōhannes wæs wanigende on his hlīsan, for þan þe hē wearð oncnāwen wītega, sē þe wæs lytle ær Crīst geteald
Beó ā getreówra þonne þē mon tō wēne, þȳ læs men wēnan þæt þū nāne næbbe būton wið hlīsan (unless you get credit for it)
Wilnigaþ monige men anwealdes þe hié woldon habban gōdne hlīsan, þeáh hī his unwyrþe sién
Næfre hlīsan āh Meotud þan māran þonne hē wið monna bearn wyrceð weldædum
quotations.english: no more glorious attribute has the Maker than his mercy to man

sub_senses.label: (2 a)
sub_senses.heading: where special characteristics are attributed, reputation

sub_senses.label: (α)
sub_senses.heading: for something, the thing expressed (or implied) by a noun

quotations.old_english: Hlīsa rumusculus (speciali castimonia)
Hlīse singalre opinio crebra (lectionis assiduitate)
Wilnung ungemetlices hlīsan gōdra weorca
Hī willað habban þone hlīsan hālgidōmes odorem de se extendere sanctae opinionis quaerunt

sub_senses.label: (β)
sub_senses.heading: of being or doing something, with clause

quotations.old_english: His hlīsa weóx . . . þæt hē sōð God wæs
Ne hē ne scrīfe þæs hlīsan būton hū hē ryhtosð wyrce
For þām gōdan hlīsan (þæt hié gifule þyncen)
Monige menn noldan þone hlīsan habban þæt hié unwīse sién, nonnulli aestimari hebetes nolunt

Monig mon dēð micel fæsten, and hæfð þone hlīsan þæt hē hit dō for forhæfdnesse . . . monig bið āgīeta his gōda, and wilnaþ mid þȳ geearnigan þone hlīsan þæt hē sié rūmgiful saepe sub parsimoniae nomine se tenacia palliat, contraque se effusio sub appetta-tione largitatis occultat
Hē wæs . . . beorn bōca gleáw. Boitius se hæle hātte, sē þone hlīsan geþah
Þone eádegan hlīsan faustam famam (Ald. 161, 12)

sub_senses.heading: report of those who no longer exist

quotations.old_english: Hwæt is hiora here būton se hlīsa ān ?

sub_senses.heading: what is told about a person

quotations.old_english: Nis ūs se hlīsa tō forswigianne þe be þām eádegan Gregorie þurh ealdra manna sage tō ūs becōm nec silentio praetereunda opinio, quae de beato Gregorio traditione maiorum ad nos usque perlata est

sub_senses.label: (l)
sub_senses.heading: fame of something admirable or remarkable

quotations.old_english: Se gesæliga hlīsa hire geornfulnesse felix industriae eius rumor
